title: Quality Analyst: single-video script, Shorts and visual plan

criteria.check: The first 15 seconds open on the most dramatic moment or consequence, then state the question, then a one-line promise. No channel intro.
criteria.why: Viewers decide in the first seconds; the format lives on one strong question.

criteria.check: The script follows its format's spine (for example a running clock for day_by_day, rounds and verdicts for versus) and escalates block by block.
criteria.why: A structure the viewer can feel keeps them watching.

criteria.check: The ending answers the opening question and names the next video.
criteria.why: An unanswered promise loses trust; the bridge drives the next view.

criteria.check: Every scene is one visual beat of 10 to 25 words (4 to 10 seconds); no scene carries two ideas.
criteria.why: A visual change every few seconds is the format.

criteria.check: Claims are concrete and scaled to the viewer (comparisons, second person); no vague 'a lot', 'many', 'huge'.
criteria.why: Concrete images are what an infographic can show.

criteria.check: About 55-65 % illustration, 25-35 % data and 5-10 % stinger scenes; never more than three data scenes or two stingers in a row.
criteria.why: Variety keeps the rhythm; long chart runs feel like a lecture.

criteria.check: Every reveal (bar, pin, list row, character, callout) is cued to the word that names it.
criteria.why: Reveals on the word make the motion feel deliberate.

criteria.check: Each frame prompt says where each figure stands and how big it is, names things by their specific type, and fits the scene's narration.
criteria.why: Vague placement gives cropped, garbled or wrong pictures.

criteria.check: Animated frames are the key beats only (hook, turning point, climax), each with one simple main motion moving the way the subject faces.
criteria.why: Complex or misdirected motion comes out wrong and wastes the cap.

criteria.check: Each Short has its hook in the first sentence, 90-130 words, exactly one data scene, and stands alone without the long video.
A viewer with no background can follow it: terms are explained once, in plain words, before they are used.
Speculation (what_if, forecasts) is labelled as such once, early, and kept visibly apart from facts; no paraphrase is presented as a quotation.
criteria.why: The channel's credibility rests on it.

criteria.check: When the style or palette was chosen automatically, it suits the story's tone, subject and era, and the chart colours match the pictures' palette line, so the video looks like one piece.
criteria.why: A mismatched look reads as a template, not a story.
